dedupe_keys.name: usgs mf owhm modflow one water hydrologic flow model conjunctive use surface water groundwater and irrigation supply and demand simulation

description: MF-OWHM, also called OneWater, is the USGS MODFLOW-based conjunctive-use simulation software (Boyce 2025, version 2.3.1, DOI 10.5066/P9P8I8GS; Techniques and Methods 6-A60). Contents: an integrated hydrologic model that places physically based flow processes from MODFLOW-2005 and its variants inside a supply and demand framework: three-dimensional groundwater flow, stream, river, lake and reservoir flow, land use and crop simulation with estimated irrigation demand, reservoir operations, aquifer compaction and subsidence, seawater intrusion, karst and pipe network flow, and unsaturated flow. An interpretive S-Language lets users write custom reservoir operation rules and decision trees. Producer: USGS (S.E. Boyce and co-authors). Coverage: any basin a user builds a model for; the README notes that the first version was selected by the World Bank Water Resource Software Review as one of three recommended conjunctive-use programs. Format and access: Fortran source, 64-bit Windows and Linux executables, examples and post-processors (ZoneBudget, HydFMT) on code.usgs.gov, with a USGS landing page. Licence: Apache License 2.0 (repository licence). Caveats: setting up a model needs substantial hydrogeological data and MODFLOW expertise. Simulation uses: water supply and irrigation allocation under drought or climate scenarios, reservoir operation studies and subsidence effects on infrastructure. Related records: model-modflow-6 and model-modflow-api-agricultural-water-use-package.
